_comment: DERIVED, never hand-edited. The full truth table of flows._auth_retry_allowed and flows.is_write_flow over every input shape that can change an answer. Regenerate with tests/test_auth_retry_truth_table.py --update. A diff here is a change to what may be re-run after an auth refresh, which is a write-safety decision: review it cell by cell.
answers: not retrying a MULTI-WRITE flow after auth refresh (a re-run would re-fire an already-landed earlier write; per-write resume is not yet supported) — run `flow login` then replay
not retrying a parameterized write after auth refresh (would risk a double-submit) — run `flow login` then replay this row; its row-keyed Idempotency-Key dedupes the re-run
not retrying a write after auth refresh without an idempotency precheck (would risk a double-submit) — add mutate.precheck_* or run `flow login` then replay

not retrying after auth refresh — 2 recorded steps are marked as WRITING, so a whole-flow precheck (which only models the LAST write) cannot tell whether an earlier one already landed, and a re-run would re-fire it. This is about the RECIPE, not the declaration: `flow inspect --name f` shows which steps are marked — if only one of them really writes, re-record so the others are not. Otherwise run `flow login` then replay

not retrying after auth refresh — a recorded step is marked as WRITING and this flow declares no write, so a re-run from the start could re-fire it with no confirm barrier to detect that. Run `flow login --name f`, then replay. `flow inspect --name f` shows WHICH step is marked (the mark can come from the wire or from the step's wording; which of the two it was is not recorded)

not retrying after auth refresh — this run's write is KNOWN to have committed (the confirm transition was observed before the failure), so a re-run from the start would fire it a second time. The failure that followed is real and needs looking at, but the write itself must not be re-driven
